transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-12
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Leah (Redwood AE), Owen (Redwood SE), Mira (Redwood SE), Daniel (CTO, SummitCore), Priya (Platform Lead), Marcus (SRE), Sofia (Security)

Summary:
Quick workshop to align on integration approach: hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment for SummitCore's conversational analytics product. Primary concerns: latency tail, multi-tenant quotas, observability hooks (token-level traces), SDK support (LangChain/LlamaIndex adapters), gateway/proxy deployment patterns, and security (SAML, KMS, audit logs). Agreed to run a pilot with perf benchmarks and a short private security review.

Topics covered:
- Current infra + traffic profile
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
- SDKs & adapter options (LangChain, LlamaIndex, and custom SDK)
- Gateway/proxy architecture and sidecar vs external proxy patterns
- Rate limits, tenant quotas, burst handling and throttling strategies
- Observability: spans, token-level cost breakdowns, tracing hooks, alerting
- Security/compliance: SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs, data residency

Transcript body (timestamps are approximate, transcription imperfect):
[00:00] Leah: okay, hey everyone thanks for joining, um, quick intros, i'll hand it to daniel to say a little about summitcore and why we're re-evaluating our stack.
[00:18] Daniel: yeah thanks leah. so SummitCore runs real-time conversational analytics over customer transcripts and we generate insights for ops and Q/A teams. Our current flow is a mix of third-party hosted endpoints and an internal inference fleet. We're looking for something that's easier to operate but gives predictable latency and cost. mainly worried about 95/99th latency, and we have to meet a strict P99 SLO of 450ms on short queries.
[00:40] Owen: got it, thanks. quick clarifying q — is that 450ms including your pre/post processing or just model inference?
[00:48] Daniel: that's end-to-end from request to model token return for the quick NER and intent checks, so includes our gateway and any KV cache lookups.
[00:58] Priya: also, we have multi-tenant constraints — each tenant gets a quota and we can burst but need per-tenant throttles and route-based quotas, and observability per-tenant.
[01:14] Leah: perfect. i want to walk through three broad options: Redwood Hosted (fast onboarding), Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem) — and then map how you'd integrate: SDKs, gateway or sidecar, or use our managed gateway.
[01:32] Mira: hi team — technical note on batching: if you have lots of short queries, we can do continuous batching with latency-aware windowing. that usually helps cost without hurting P99 if tuned. we can also pin model variants for critical tenants.
[01:49] Marcus: quick question on 'pin model variants' — does that mean i can fix a tenant to a lower-latency model even if we have a cheaper high-latency model for others?
[01:59] Owen: exactly, you can route by policy — e.g., tenant X -> low-latency quantized variant on Dedicated vs tenant Y -> hosted cheaper model. automatic fallback too if capacity is constrained.
[02:12] Priya: on SDKs — we use LangChain and a few LlamaIndex connectors. what's the recommended path to keep developer velocity?
[02:20] Mira: we have first-class SDKs that plug into LangChain and LlamaIndex, there's an adapter repo we share. it's basically a drop-in client and a small connector for the stores. sometimes the transcription mislabels it as 'Lang Chain' but it's standard.
[02:37] Daniel: will that change if we pick Private? we run some workloads on prem for compliance.
[02:44] Leah: Private is still compatible with the same SDKs — the control plane is private, and you can run the inference nodes in your VPC. The SDK just points at a different endpoint and you keep the same call patterns.
[02:56] Sofia: security — we need SAML SSO, RBAC, KMS support for our keys, and audit log granularity down to token request level. how mature are those?
[03:06] Owen: we integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, HSMs) and we have audit logs that include request metadata. note: token-level logs can be redacted or hashed, we'll work with security to define retention windows.
[03:21] Sofia: retention windows — can the logs be sent to our SIEM? we don't want audit data stored in Redwood long-term.
[03:29] Mira: yes, logs can stream to your syslog/S3/BigQuery. for private deployments you control retention; for hosted we have configurable retention policies and log-forwarding.
[03:40] Daniel: on latency — can you give a typical profile for Hosted vs Dedicated? we've seen hosted be unpredictable under burst.
[03:49] Owen: hosted is optimized for fast onboarding and steady-state loads; Dedicated is reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput and better P99 under heavy burst. Example: small TGI-like model on hosted might have a P99 around 600-800ms depending on region and load; on Dedicated with pinned kernels and optimized batching we often see P99 drop under 300-400ms for short sequences. these numbers are model and infra dependent but we can run a benchmark with your traffic.
[04:14] Priya: you mentioned batching windows — our request pattern is spiky with a lot of short requests at peak. how do you avoid tail latency with batching?
[04:24] Mira: we use adaptive batching and priority queues — critical tenants get priority and smaller windowing; background jobs are batched more aggressively. also prefix KV caching reduces tokens served for repeated contexts.
[04:36] Marcus: you said KV caching — our infra team called it KV cash earlier in a note — what gets cached exactly?
[04:42] Owen: yeah, sorry, KV cache — caching the model's key/value states for repeated contexts so you don't recompute prompts from scratch. it's safe for deterministic prompts and can be per-tenant.
[04:53] Leah: question for summitcore — what's your expected qps and average tokens per request for short queries vs longer summaries?
[05:00] Priya: short queries ~120 reqs/sec at peak across tenants, avg 12 tokens in/out; longer summaries are low qps ~6-8 reqs/sec but 800-1500 tokens.
[05:12] Owen: excellent, that mix is helpful — short-query tail is the hard one. we'll propose Dedicated pool sizing for the short-query peak and recommend a hosted fallback for overflow to control cost.
[05:23] Daniel: on proxy/gateway — we currently have an edge gateway that signs requests and does tenant routing. is the recommended pattern to put Redwood behind our gateway, or deploy a sidecar per service?
[05:34] Mira: both patterns are valid. sidecar gives you tighter network control and lower hop latency if you're co-located with inference nodes in your VPC. managed gateway is simpler: you call a regional managed endpoint and we handle rate limiting, token billing, and routing. many customers use a hybrid: sidecar for internal traffic and managed gateway for external/low-sensitivity flows.
[05:55] Marcus: if we use a sidecar, do we need to run any special orchestration? e.g., helm charts or k8s operator?
[06:02] Owen: we provide a lightweight helm chart and a deployment example. for Private on-prem we also offer an operator but most customers run the sidecar as a small deployment with an RBAC token to call the private control plane.
[06:15] Priya: quotas — can you enforce per-route and per-tenant quotas, and do you expose the quota usage in the console and via APIs?
[06:24] Mira: yes. per-route, per-tenant, and per-key quotas. console shows token/req usage by tenant and model, and we expose APIs and webhooks for quota events so you can throttle upstream and show user-facing messages.
[06:36] Leah: quick note about cost control — we can recommend quantization profiles and suggest model variants to hit cost targets. Redwood Optimize will suggest batch sizes and quant profiles based on your workload.
[06:46] Daniel: you mentioned fallback to hosted when Dedicated is saturated — how are tokens billed in that case? does billing split across pools?
[06:53] Owen: we meter per-model/per-pool, and the billing lines will show pool-level attribution. During overflow to hosted, those tokens are billed at the hosted rates for that model variant. we'll include cost attribution in the pilot analysis.
[07:06] Priya: observability: how granular are traces? can we see per-token latencies and which kernel was used?
[07:13] Mira: yes, our console provides per-token cost and latency breakdown, and tracing hooks include kernel selection metadata, sequence length, and batching window. you can send traces to your tracing backend or view in Redwood Console. small caveat: some kernel metadata may be obfuscated in hosted for multi-tenant privacy, but available in Dedicated/Private.
[07:33] Sofia: security follow-up — do you support customer-managed keys so the model tokens never leave our control?
[07:39] Owen: with Private deployments you manage keys entirely; with Dedicated we can integrate with your KMS so data at rest can be encrypted with your keys. For hosted we support envelope encryption with customer-managed KMS keys.
[07:51] Daniel: what's the onboarding timeline? if we decide on Dedicated for the pilot, how long to provision?
[07:58] Leah: for Dedicated it's typically 2-4 weeks to provision reserved pools and run initial bench. Private (VPC) can be 3-6 weeks depending on network approval and on-prem setup. Hosted is immediate. For the pilot we usually do a 4-week engagement: 1 week onboarding and config, 1 week perf bench, 1 week integration + observability checks, 1 week security review and wrap-up.
[08:23] Marcus: during benchmark, will we be able to exercise our traffic shapes and measure P99?
[08:28] Owen: yes, we can run your traffic profile and capture p50/p95/p99, cost per token, and error rates. we'll also test canary rollouts and automatic fallback.
[08:37] Priya: do you have any public benchmarks or do you run them per-customer?
[08:41] Leah: we publish curated model profiles but for real production numbers we always run a customer-specific benchmark. we'll put the sample template in the shared folder.
[08:50] Daniel: one more question on integrations — we use LlamaIndex heavily for vector DB connectors. does Redwood support embedding pipelines and offline embedding jobs?
[08:58] Mira: yes, embedding pipelines are supported. we have batching for embedding jobs and connectors for common vector stores. you can run embeddings in Dedicated or Hosted; for large offline jobs we can recommend a cheap compute pool.
[09:10] Sofia: on legal/comms — is there an NDA addendum for security scans?
[09:14] Leah: yes, we have a security addendum and can do an on-site or hosted scan depending on scope. we'll loop in legal after this call.
[09:22] Owen: small note — our SDKs include retry semantics, idempotency keys, and per-request metadata fields so you can carry tenant id, trace id, and any routing hints.
[09:33] Priya: that sounds good, we want a simple path to swap in the SDK with minimal code changes.
[09:37] Mira: we'll send a LangChain/LlamaIndex adapter example and a short integration guide.
[09:42] Daniel: awesome. next steps?
[09:45] Leah: recap — Redwood sends pilot SOW + pricing + benchmark plan; SummitCore shares traffic profile and sample prompts; Owen to sketch a Dedicated pool config and batching profile; Sofia to start security artifact list. We target the first pilot week starting 2027-03-22 if approvals go through.
[10:05] Marcus: noted. thanks for the clarity.
[10:08] Leah: thanks everyone, i'll follow up with the deck and links — shared artifacts: https://redwood.com/summitcore/pilot-deck (deck), https://redwood.com/shared/bench-template.csv (traffic template), security addendum link (internal).
[10:22] Daniel: thanks all. bye.
